title: Inheritance and abstract classes

notes: Animal is abstract: it can't be made on its own.
sound() is abstract: every animal must provide one.
Goat adds to describe() with super.describe() instead of copying it.
The loop treats both as Animal; each still uses its own sound().

exercises.title: Slime, Archer, Golem
exercises.prompt: Enemy is finished. Complete the three children: Slime (name "Slime", 20 health, attackPower 3); Archer ("Archer", 35 health, attackPower 7, and describe() adds " [ranged]" to the parent's text using super.describe()); Golem ("Golem", 80 health, attackPower 12, and its stone skin halves damage: override takeDamage to call super.takeDamage(amount / 2)).

tests.call: new Slime().attackPower() + new Archer().attackPower() + new Golem().attackPower()
((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Golem g = new Golem(); g.takeDamage(30); return g.describe(); }).get()
tests.name: stone skin

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Enemy e = new Golem(); e.takeDamage(500); return e.getHealth() + " " + e.isAlive(); }).get()
tests.name: golem can still fall

tests.why: Archer should build on the parent's describe() with super.describe().
Golem should call super.takeDamage(...) rather than copy the code.

hints: Each constructor just calls super with the right name and health: super("Slime", 20);
Archer: @Override public String describe() { return super.describe() + " [ranged]"; }
Golem: @Override public void takeDamage(int amount) { super.takeDamage(amount / 2); }

exercises.title: Group savings account
exercises.prompt: Account is finished. Write class GroupSavings extends Account with constructor GroupSavings(String owner, double opening, double ratePercent). Overrides: withdraw(double amount) returns false if amount is more than half the balance, otherwise uses the parent's withdraw (super.withdraw); summary() adds " (group, 2.0%)" (the rate) to the parent's summary. New method monthEnd() adds the monthly interest: balance × (1 + rate/100), rounded to 2 decimals.

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { GroupSavings g = new GroupSavings("Wanjiru", 1000, 2); return g.withdraw(600) + " " + g.withdraw(500) + " " + g.getBalance(); }).get()
tests.name: only half can leave

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { GroupSavings g = new GroupSavings("Wanjiru", 1000, 2); g.monthEnd(); return g.getBalance() + ""; }).get()
tests.name: interest

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Account a = new GroupSavings("Amina", 800, 1); return a.withdraw(500) + ""; }).get()
tests.name: override works through an Account variable

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { GroupSavings g = new GroupSavings("Juma", 333.33, 1.5); g.monthEnd(); return g.getBalance() + ""; }).get()
tests.name: rounding

tests.why: Reuse the parent's checks with super.withdraw(amount).

hints: Store the rate in a private final double field.
@Override public boolean withdraw(double amount) { if (amount > balance / 2) return false; return super.withdraw(amount); }

exercises.title: Turrets
exercises.prompt: abstract class Turret holds the ammo. Write its final fire(): if ammo is less than ammoPerShot() return 0; otherwise subtract ammoPerShot() and return damage(). Write fireAll(): keep firing until a shot returns 0, and return the total damage. The constructor throws IllegalArgumentException for negative ammo. Children: Cannon(int ammo) does 40 damage using 2 ammo per shot; Laser(int ammo) does 15 damage using 1 ammo per shot.

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Cannon c = new Cannon(5); return c.fire() + " " + c.fire() + " " + c.fire() + " " + c.getAmmo(); }).get()
tests.name: cannon

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { int total = 0; for (Turret t : java.util.List.of(new Cannon(4), new Laser(2))) total += t.fireAll(); return total + ""; }).get()
tests.name: a list of turrets

hints: fire(): if (ammo < ammoPerShot()) return 0; ammo -= ammoPerShot(); return damage();
fireAll(): int total = 0; int d; while ((d = fire()) > 0) total += d; return total;
The children only return numbers: damage() { return 40; } ammoPerShot() { return 2; }

quiz.q: What must the first line of a child constructor be when the parent has only Enemy(String, int)?
quiz.why: The parent must be built first, with arguments it accepts.

choices: The compiler errors if you didn't really override (e.g. a typo)
It's required for abstract methods only
quiz.why: It turns a silent mistake into a compile error.

quiz.q: Archer's describe() returns super.describe() + " [ranged]". What does super.describe() run?
A Tractor needs an Engine. Best design?
choices: Tractor has a field of type Engine (composition)
Copy the engine code into Tractor
quiz.why: A tractor HAS an engine; it isn't one.

choices: has a body the child may use
has no body; every concrete child must write it
quiz.why: That's how the parent leaves a blank for children.

cards.q: How many classes can a class extend?

cards.a: Visible to child classes (and the same package), not everyone.

cards.q: Call the parent's version of a method?
Inheritance vs composition rule of thumb?
cards.a: 'is a' -> extends; 'has a' -> a field. Prefer composition when unsure.

explain: Explain when you would use inheritance and when composition, with one example of each from a game or farm program you make up.
